clue.text: A case of up sticks, man, in old solver's mansion — bear with monopoly

indicators.note: the word man is placed in the middle of the archaic word for the solver, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: THOU is the old form of 'you', the person solving
HE is a man, by the pronoun
a SEAT is a country mansion, as in a family seat
POOH is A. A. Milne's bear
to CORNER a market is to hold a monopoly in it

explanation.surface: A muddled description of an old mansion with a bear and a board game, all in one breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the book's story in which Eeyore's house of sticks is taken up and moved to Pooh Corner; the book also introduced the game of Poohsticks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Milne book tells how a stick-built house was picked up and rebuilt at a new spot, a case of sticks going up.

clue.text: God includes student in scheme

indicators.note: the god's name holds the student's letter inside it

parts.note: PAN is the Greek god of the wild
L is a learner, from the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A deity draws a pupil into some grand design.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme and a plan are synonyms: an arrangement for doing something.

clue.text: Author of work of reference dealing with malt etc

definitions.meaning: E. Cobham ... compiled ... Dictionary of Phrase and Fable
someone who makes beer from malt and hops

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Victorian compiler of a famous reference dictionary, and a maker of beer from malt.

clue.text: Impermanent character, legendary if offensive

definitions.meaning: a figure built of snow melts away soon after it is made
the Abominable one is the legendary yeti; abominable means offensive

explanation.definitionFit: A snow figure melts away, and the Himalayan legend is called the Abominable one, abominable meaning offensive.

clue.text: Bad dog Henry, periodic 20

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the two words are in a poor, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A naughty dog called Henry who misbehaves at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer TABLE TOP, so the definition reads 'periodic table top': the first element in the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The lightest element has atomic number one, so it sits first, at the top of the periodic table.

clue.text: Exceed in wickedness (like Parolles) away from home, house and home

parts.note: a team playing an away match is OUT, not at home
a VILLA is a house
IN means at home

explanation.surface: Parolles, the braggart soldier of Shakespeare, is the model of out-doing others in roguery, at home or away.
explanation.walkthrough: In All's Well That Ends Well Parolles is said to have 'out-villained villainy so far' that his rarity redeems him.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean coinage meaning to surpass someone in villainy, used of Parolles in All's Well.

clue.text: Mushroom made of silver has one getting a lot of money

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum
A means one

indicators.note: a lot of signals that only part of the word for money is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: RICHES means money or wealth

explanation.surface: A mushroom of silver brings someone a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' keeps only RIC, the first half of RICHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Agarics are the gilled mushrooms, the family including the field mushroom and fly agaric.

clue.text: Cold bird, one might say, is the issue …

indicators.note: signals the words are to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a chilled wren is a cold bird

explanation.surface: A frozen bird is the problem to discuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' wants to mean a problem, but here it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring or descendants.

clue.text: See 10
… Bird among women shortly, going to jug, each of you no good — in our 17

indicators.note: the bird is placed among the abbreviated women, between them

parts.note: W is short for women; two of them for the plural
a HEN is a bird
a EWER is a water jug
EVERY means each

explanation.surface: A hen among some women heads off to a jug, with each of you being useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is INFANCY, so the definition is 'in our infancy'; this title is Milne's book of children's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Milne's poetry collection's title says when something happened: in childhood, in our infancy.

clue.text: See 10
Sheep or goat's royal request in 10 11 9

definitions.meaning: a ram or billy goat is one that butts with its head
in Milne's poem The King's Breakfast the King asks for a little bit of it for the royal slice of bread

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an animal that rams with its head, and the spread the King wants in a Milne poem.

clue.text: Stumble on fib about pet (repeated twice)

parts.note: to TRIP is to stumble

indicators.note: the fib goes round the pet

parts.note: a LIE is a fib
a CAT is a pet

explanation.surface: Someone trips over a lie concerning their pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just puts one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done once and repeated twice exists in three copies, in triplicate.

clue.text: Very good article on candied stalks

definitions.note: plural stalks define the plant whose stalks are candied, a mass noun

parts.note: ANGELIC means very good, well behaved
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay about crystallised fruit stems is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant's stems are candied and used green to decorate cakes.

clue.text: Information is given by volunteers after they follow 2 with broom

parts.note: GEN is slang for information
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers pass on news and then sweep up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after they follow 2' is a hint: PLAN (2) followed by TA ('they') and the answer gives PLANTA GENISTA, the Latin name for broom behind the Plantagenets.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the botanical genus of the broom shrubs, yellow-flowered.

clue.text: Guardian's attempt to hide note on drink going up

indicators.note: the attempt conceals the other pieces inside itself

parts.note: a TRY is an attempt
UT is the old name for the note doh

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the drink is read upward, backwards

parts.note: ALE is a drink

explanation.surface: A protector tries to stash a drink before it rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelary means acting as a protector, as a tutelary deity watches over a place.

clue.text: First stage at home for the Dream?

parts.note: IN means at home
to fancy is to dream of something, and a fancy is a dream

explanation.surface: Staying in for the Dream, perhaps Shakespeare's comedy at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Babyhood is the earliest stage of a person's life.

clue.text: Split in the church which holds minister an idiot

indicators.note: the church contains the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
REV is short for reverend, a minister
an ASS is an idiot

explanation.surface: A schism in the church whose vicar is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a church schism but is a deep crack in a glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep crack or fissure in a glacier's ice is a split.

clue.text: Final comment serves to keep it a philosophical issue

indicators.note: the answer's letters issue, or come out, from within these words

explanation.surface: A last remark serves to keep a philosophical question alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun after 'philosophical', but it signals letters coming out of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The words on a tombstone are the last thing said about someone.

clue.text: Put it on trestles to make pill work

parts.note: a TABLET is a pill
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Laying out remedies on trestles to make up medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: A board laid on trestles gives a flat top surface like a table's.

clue.text: See 1
Hypocrite's movement?

definitions.meaning: one who cants, that is talks hypocritically
a horse's gait between trot and gallop

explanation.definitionFit: One who speaks cant is a hypocrite; a horse moving between trot and gallop also does this gait.

clue.text: See 1
Society thief, maybe either 24

parts.note: a PECULATOR is an embezzler, one who steals entrusted funds

explanation.surface: A society thief may be either a bull or a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is both BEAR (across) and BULL (down): both are stock market traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulls and bears on the stock market are both people who gamble on price moves.

clue.text: Have 8 to tolerate

definitions.meaning: 8 is CHILDREN; to give birth to them

explanation.definitionFit: To give birth to offspring, and to put up with something, are two senses of one verb.

clue.text: Sign in the centre

explanation.definitionFit: Taurus the zodiac sign, and the central target on a dartboard, both bear this name.

clue.text: One with swimming ability more exaggerated?

parts.note: OTT is over the top, exaggerated
ER is the comparative ending meaning more

explanation.surface: Who is the more extravagant swimmer?
explanation.definitionFit: A river mammal that swims superbly.

clue.text: Unique, unlike the upper house

definitions.meaning: the House of Lords is full of peers; without them is the opposite

explanation.definitionFit: Without equal, and lacking lords, the House of Lords being made of peers.
